title: Open Table Formats: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Open Table Formats: Visual Guide

1. The Missing Layer | the catalog to snapshot to manifest to file tree, with each ACID letter tappable to show which layer supplies it | atomicity comes from committing one small authoritative reference after immutable data is written, and table ACID does not make a multi-table workflow atomic

2. Walking The Chain | six snapshots with their operations and row counts, readable as-of, plus a retention slider that expires history under a pinned experiment | a snapshot is an immutable table state and time travel by ID is deterministic where timestamps are not, and expiring history breaks pinned jobs at read time

3. Safe Or Breaking | seven schema changes classified under an ID-aware reader and a name-only tool, including a rename whose verdict flips | field IDs make renames and reordering safe for ID-aware readers, while adding a required column, dropping, narrowing and recycling an identifier are breaking under any reader

4. Backfill Without Mutating | the five-step safe backfill with what the table looks like at each step, plus the mixed-logic problem for very large backfills | a backfill pins its input snapshot, stages outputs invisibly, validates against the current snapshot and publishes once, so failure leaves orphans rather than partial state

5. The Atomic Alias | a search index rebuild in five phases with the alias contents shown, plus four ways to route writes during the cutover | an index rebuild is publish-by-pointer with different nouns, and switching only the read alias makes the two generations diverge invisibly
